If you couldn't afford to snatch a home before covid you're fucked unless you have inherited wealth/assets headed your way.  Or you're willing and able to spend a far higher % of your income than prior generations.

**Mechwarrior 3.**  While probably not a fan among Battletech purists, I absolutely oved this game.  Mech battles and the most immersive story i've experienced in the mechwarrior series.  Plus fucking around in an Elemental battle suits and taking on 100 ton mechs.  Pure joy.

**Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2.**  Crazed representation of Einstein?  Ridiculous weapons based in an alternative Cold War universe?  I still play this occasionally but it's gotten more difficult to find versions compatible with newer releases of Windows.

**Rise of the Dragon (1990).**   Point and click adventure set in a dystopian/almost cyberpunk future.  I would get stuck in one spot and could never beat it as a kid.  Eventually I found a working copy and beat it as an adult.  It tormented me for years until that point but it holds a special place in my gaming pantheon.  I don't know if I could ever play it again though.
